n01.q: In “She looks ___ today”, which word is correct?
n01.e: look is a linking verb, so it is followed by an adjective: happy.

n01.q: What part of speech is “fast” in “He drives fast”?
n01.e: fast describes how he drives (the verb), so it is an adverb.

n01.q: What part of speech is “drink” in “I need a drink”?
n01.e: After the article a, drink is a noun.

n01.q: Which sentence uses the pattern S + V + O + O?
n01.e: gave has two objects: me (indirect) and a book (direct).

n01.q: Which word is a linking verb?
n01.e: seem links the subject to a complement: He seems tired.
taste is a linking verb here, so an adjective follows.

n01.q: In “Wow! That was amazing!”, “Wow” is a(n) ___.
In “She bought those books”, which word is a determiner?
n01.e: those comes before the noun books and points to specific things: a determiner.

n02.e: Short CVC word: double the final consonant.
its (no apostrophe) shows possession; it's means it is.

o: Sokha, my friend, lives in Takeo.
Sokha my friend, lives in Takeo.
Sokha, my friend lives in Takeo.
Sokha my friend lives, in Takeo.
n02.e: Commas go around the extra information, my friend.
i before e except after c.
Many words ending in -o after a consonant add -es: potatoes.
Languages and nationalities begin with a capital: Khmer.

n03.q: The ___ of the new school was a great success. (complete)
n03.e: After the, a noun is needed: completion.
Before a noun, use an adjective: successful.
An adverb describes the verb: carefully.
In a compound adjective before a noun, the unit is singular.

n03.q: We should ___ the rules to make them easier. (simple)

n04.q: She has ___ a letter to her friend.

n04.e: Past simple of drink is drank.

n04.q: The thief was ___ by the police.
The window was ___ by the ball.
I ___ the book on the table yesterday.
Which verb has the same form in V1, V2 and V3?

n05.q: Look at the black clouds! It ___ rain.
n05.e: A prediction from present evidence uses be going to.

n05.q: I ___ Dara at five o'clock tomorrow. We have already arranged it.
I will phone you when I ___ home.
n05.e: After when, use a present tense for the future.

n05.q: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home.
n05.e: No will in an if clause.
be about to means very soon.
A decision made earlier: be going to.

n06.q: When I was a child, I ___ in Kampot.
n06.e: used to + V1 for a past state.

n06.q: Every summer we ___ to our grandparents' village.
n06.e: would + V1 for repeated past actions.

n06.q: Did you ___ play football when you were young?
It took me a while to get used to ___ the heat.
Which sentence is correct for a past state?
o: I would have long hair when I was young.
I used to have long hair.
I am used to have long hair.
I use to have long hair now.
n06.e: have is a state verb, so used to is needed (not would).

n06.q: I ___ in Phnom Penh for five years.
n06.e: A period of stated length: Past Simple.

n06.q: He ___ smoke, but he stopped last year.
n06.e: used to + V1 for a past habit that has ended.

n07.e: know is a stative verb: no continuous form.

n07.q: She ___ emails all morning, so she is tired.
n07.e: Duration of an activity: Present Perfect Continuous.
A completed number of things: Present Perfect Simple.

n07.q: When I arrived, the class ___ already ___.
n07.e: The earlier past action: Past Perfect.

n07.q: He ___ a shower when the phone rang.
n07.e: An action in progress interrupted by another: Past Continuous.

o: I am having lunch with my friend.
n07.e: have meaning eat can be continuous; have meaning possess cannot.

n08.q: You ___ park here. It is forbidden.
You ___ come tomorrow. It's a holiday.
She isn't answering. She ___ be asleep.
He ___ have left already. His coat has gone.
n08.e: Strong past deduction: must have + V3.

n08.q: The answer is wrong. It ___ be correct.
n08.e: Almost certain that it is not true: can't.

n08.q: You ___ have told me earlier. Now it is too late.
n08.e: should have + V3 = past criticism or regret.

n08.q: I ___ finish the test in time. It was hard but I did it.
n08.e: A specific past achievement: was able to.

n08.q: You ___ better hurry or you'll miss the bus.
I ___ rather stay at home tonight.

n08.e: Modal + base verb; no to, no -s.

n09.q: I wish I ___ harder last year.
n09.e: Regret about the past: wish + Past Perfect.
wish + would for annoyance about someone's behavior.

n09.q: He talks as if he ___ everything.
n09.e: as if + past for an unreal comparison.

n09.q: You can borrow my book ___ you return it tomorrow.
___ you hurry, you will miss the train.
___ I known about the problem, I would have helped.
n09.e: Inverted third conditional: Had I known = If I had known.

n10.q: It is said that he is rich. = He ___ rich.
n10.e: Reporting passive: is said to + V1.
Perfect modal passive: should have been + V3.

n10.q: She is going to ___ her house painted.
I was ___ a book for my birthday.
n10.e: Passive with two objects: I was given a book.

n11.q: Please ___ the light. It's too bright.
I'm looking ___ my keys. Have you seen them?
We have ___ paper. Please buy some.
n11.e: run out of = have none left.

n11.q: The match was ___ because of rain.
She ___ the offer because the salary was low.

n11.e: A pronoun goes between the verb and the particle.

n12.q: He stopped ___ because it was bad for his health.
Remember ___ the door when you leave.
n12.e: remember to + V1 = do not forget.

n12.q: The teacher made us ___ the text again.
She is old enough ___ the exam.
I saw him ___ the road. (whole action)
n12.e: see + object + base verb = whole action.

n12.q: I tried ___ the window, but it was stuck.

n13.q: ___ is a book on the desk.
n13.e: There + be introduces something that exists.

n13.q: There ___ a pen and two books on the table.
n13.e: The verb agrees with the first noun: a pen.

n14.q: The ___ books are on the desk. (more than one student)
n14.e: Plural noun ending in -s + apostrophe: students' books.
Subject names ending in -s take a singular verb.

n14.q: The police ___ looking for the thief.
We have a ___ break at eleven.
n14.e: In a compound adjective, the unit stays singular.

n14.q: Tom and Mary live together. ___ house is near the school.
n14.e: Joint possession: 's after the last name.

n15.q: There are ___ students in the class today than yesterday.
I have ___ friends in this city, so I feel lonely.
She has ___ time to finish the report, so she is relaxed.
n15.e: a little = some (positive) with uncountable nouns.

n15.q: Each of the students ___ a book.
n15.e: each of + plural noun takes a singular verb.

n15.q: ___ answer is correct. They are both wrong. (two answers)
n15.e: neither = not one and not the other.

n15.q: One pen is red; ___ is blue.
n15.e: the other = the second of two.

n15.q: Some students like tea; ___ prefer coffee.

n16.q: I am ___ in this lesson. It is not interesting.

n16.e: A frequency adverb goes before the main verb.
A frequency adverb goes after be.
Do not put an adverb between a verb and its direct object.

n16.q: The lesson was ___ difficult that nobody finished.

n17.q: This book is ___ than that one.
This test is ___ than the last one.
The ___ you practise, the better you become.
It's the best film I ___ seen.

n17.e: worse and worse = comparative + and + comparative.

n17.q: This bag is ___ expensive as that one.

n18.e: Use any- in a negative sentence.

n18.q: Between you and ___, I think he is wrong.
I live ___. I don't share the house.

n19.e: Jobs take a / an; teacher starts with a consonant sound.
No article with most single countries.

n19.q: I'd like to be ___ honest person.
n19.e: honest starts with a vowel sound: an.

n19.q: He goes to ___ school by bike. (He is a student.)
n19.e: school used for its main purpose: no article.

n19.q: She saw a dog. ___ dog was big.
He is ___ best student in the class.

n19.e: The United States has a union name: the.

n20.e: discuss takes a direct object: no preposition.

n20.q: I arrived ___ Phnom Penh at noon.

n21.q: The student ___ book was lost is absent.
My sister, ___ lives in Kampot, is a nurse.
n21.e: Non-defining clause about a person: who.

n21.q: The man ___ lives next door is kind.
n21.e: The pronoun is the subject; do not repeat it.

n21.q: The book ___ I bought is useful. Which word can be left out?
n21.e: The pronoun that is the object, so it can be omitted.

n21.q: He passed the exam, ___ surprised everyone.
n21.e: which refers to the whole clause.

n21.q: The man ___ there is my teacher. (reduced clause)
This is the school ___ I studied.
The woman to ___ I spoke was kind.
The year ___ I graduated was important.

n22.e: V-ing for an action at the same time.

n22.q: ___ the exam, she left the room.

o: Walking down the street, the rain started.
Walked down the street, it rained.
Walk down the street, rain started.
Walking down the street, I felt rain.
n22.e: The subject of both parts must be the same.

n22.q: ___ in 1990, the book is still popular.
___ tired, she went to bed early.
Which sentence has a dangling participle?
o: Walking home, I saw my friend.
n22.e: The rain was not walking, so the subject does not match.

n23.e: Present tense in a time clause.

n23.q: ___ I was sleeping, the phone rang.
By the time I arrived, they ___.
By the time you arrive, I ___.
n23.e: by the time + present → Future Perfect.

n23.q: Finish the report ___ Friday. (not later than)

n23.e: until = up to the time that.

n24.q: It was ___ a hot day that we stayed inside.
It was ___ hot that we stayed inside.
She is ___ to vote, so she can register.
I study ___ I can pass the exam.
There were ___ many students that we had no space.

n24.e: However begins a new sentence with a comma.

n24.q: We don't have ___ time to finish.

n25.e: Auxiliary before the subject after Never.

n25.q: Not only ___ sing, but she also danced.
Hardly ___ arrived when it began to rain.
___ I known, I would have helped.
It was Sophea ___ won the prize.
No sooner had she arrived ___ it started to rain.

n26.e: A short answer repeats the auxiliary.
I hope not = I hope it will not rain.
Same auxiliary as the statement: have.

n27.e: Statement word order in an indirect question.

n27.q: Do you know ___ he is coming?
“What is she like?” asks about her ___.
n27.e: What … like? asks for a description.

n27.q: How ___ is it from here to the market?

n28.q: He told ___ that he was late.
He asked if I ___ come to the party.
“Study hard,” said the teacher. → The teacher told us ___ hard.
He said that water ___ at 100°C. (general truth)
n28.e: No backshift for a general truth.

n28.q: “I must go,” she said. → She said she ___ go.

o: Because it rained, we stayed home.
n29.e: The first has a main clause.

n29.q: Which sentence has a comma splice?
o: I was tired, so I went to bed.
I was tired, I went to bed.
I was tired; I went to bed.
I was tired. I went to bed.
n29.e: Two independent clauses are joined only by a comma.

n29.q: Choose the sentence with parallel structure.
o: She likes swimming, to run and cycling.
She likes to swim, running and cycling.
She likes swimming, running and cycling.
She likes swim, running and to cycle.
n29.e: The list items are all -ing forms.

o: He studied hard, so he passed.
n29.e: No punctuation or conjunction joins the clauses.

o: He is both smart and works hard.
He is both smart and hardworking.
He is both smartly and hardworking.
He is both smart and to work hard.
n29.e: Both … and joins two parallel items.

n29.q: Which sentence has a dangling modifier?
o: Walking home, I felt the rain.
n29.e: The rain was not walking home.

o: She was tired, but she worked.
Tired as she was, she worked.
n29.e: A dependent clause cannot stand alone.
